Veterans earned every benefit, but too often get lost in bureaucratic red tape. Events like this are a start—but real support means slashing the VA’s bloated admin costs and redirecting funds directly to those who served.

The Promoting Community-Based Prevention Services Act shows how targeted funding can work when done right. Now apply that efficiency to veteran care: cut the middlemen, prioritize service over paperwork, and ensure every dollar reaches heroes instead of bureaucrats.

Veterans’ Wellness Days are crucial, but let’s not ignore the systemic failures. Over 1,200 vets showed up at Fort Worth’s Summer VetFest in June—many waited 55 years to file claims. Why? Bureaucratic red tape and poor outreach.

Gregory Reynolds asked why there’s no toll-free number for vets who can’t travel—valid point. Events are a start, but real support means slashing VA inefficiency, not just photo ops.

Cut the bloat, streamline benefits, and put veterans first without the D.C. runaround.
